rows: A Radiant Turret Lit by the Midsummer Midnight Sun
This photograph from the Australasian Antarctic Expedition shows an ice tower glowing in the midnight sun. In the Antarctic summer the sun never sets, and the ice turns gold and pink.
What would it be like if the sun never set?
Olympic Athletes' Parade on Fifth Avenue, 1912
American athletes parade up New York's Fifth Avenue in August 1912 after returning from the Stockholm Olympics. Crowds lined the street to cheer.
How would you welcome home a champion?
Mountain Laurel, Woodstock, New York
A postcard-style photograph of mountain laurel in bloom at Woodstock, New York, in 1912. The pink and white flowers cover the shrub in late spring.
What time of year do you think this was taken?
Jim Thorpe Greeted by Mayor Gaynor

Jim Thorpe, a Sauk and Fox athlete, won the pentathlon and decathlon at the 1912 Olympics and was greeted by New York Mayor William Gaynor in the summer of 1912. The next year Thorpe lost his medals over a technicality, and they were restored in 1983.
Why would someone lose a medal for something minor?
Vaslav Nijinsky in Scheherazade
Auguste Bert photographed the great Russian dancer Vaslav Nijinsky in his role in the ballet Scheherazade around 1913. Nijinsky was famous for his leaps, which seemed to hang in the air.
How high can you jump?
Vaslav Nijinsky in Le Spectre de la Rose
Auguste Bert photographed Nijinsky in the ballet Le Spectre de la Rose, The Phantom of the Rose, in 1913. He danced the ghost of a rose that a young girl had worn to a ball.
How would you dance like a flower?
Percy MacKaye as Alwyn, the Poet
Arnold Genthe made an autochrome of the poet Percy MacKaye in costume as Alwyn in a masque, a kind of costume play. The picture is seen in a mirror view.
Why would a poet dress up as a character?
Aurora Anchored to Floe-Ice
Frank Hurley photographed the ship Aurora anchored to floe ice off the Western Base in Antarctica during the 1911 to 1914 expedition of Douglas Mawson. The ship is tiny among the ice.
Why would a ship tie up to ice?
Jim Thorpe, the Olympic Hero

Underwood and Underwood photographed Jim Thorpe in 1913, the year after his Olympic victories. Thorpe was a member of the Sauk and Fox Nation, and many call him the greatest all-round athlete in history.
What sports do you think he played?
Ann Murdock with Buzzer
Arnold Genthe photographed the actress Ann Murdock in 1914. A buzzer was a name for a small telephone-like gadget used on stage.
What would a buzzer do in a play?
French Colonial Troops, 1914
Dutch archives hold this photograph of French troops from the colonies wearing white uniforms and red caps in 1914, at the start of World War I. Soldiers from Africa and Asia fought for France.
Why would soldiers from far away fight in this war?
Eiffel Tower from the Trocadéro, Autochrome
Auguste Léon photographed the Eiffel Tower in color around 1914 for the Archives of the Planet, a project funded by the banker Albert Kahn. He wanted to record the whole world in color photographs.
What would you put in an archive of the planet?
Woman Marching with Peace Sign
A woman carries a peace sign and a U.S. flag in a march in Washington, D.C., in 1914. Peace marches began as World War I started in Europe.
What would you write on a peace sign?
Endurance Beset in Ice

Frank Hurley photographed Ernest Shackleton's ship Endurance stuck in the ice of the Weddell Sea in 1915 from far across the floe. The ice would later crush the ship, and the crew survived on the floes for months.
What would you do if your ship was stuck in ice?
Hussey and James Working in the Laboratory on Endurance
Frank Hurley photographed scientists Leonard Hussey and Reginald James working in the lab on board Endurance in 1915. Even on an expedition they did science.
What experiments would you do on a ship?
Looking Across Newly Formed Ice with Endurance
Hurley photographed new ice stretching to the ship Endurance in the Weddell Sea in 1915. A thin crust of ice formed around the ship.
What does new ice look like?
King Penguin with Young
Frank Hurley photographed a king penguin with its chick on the Shackleton expedition around 1915. King penguin chicks are fluffy and brown, and the parents keep them warm.
Why are baby penguins fluffy?
4th Field Artillery, Mexican Expedition, 1916
The U.S. Army sent soldiers into Mexico in 1916 to chase Pancho Villa. This photograph shows the 4th Field Artillery on the march.
Why would an army carry cannons on a horse-drawn wagon?
New Hope School, near Shawnee, Oklahoma
Lewis Hine photographed a rural school in Oklahoma in 1916, with 31 pupils present. Hine photographed children in school as well as at work for the National Child Labor Committee.
What would a one-room school be like?
Ruth St. Denis in an Oriental Dance
Arnold Genthe made an autochrome of the dancer Ruth St. Denis in a costume from The Book of Eastern Nights in 1916. She was a pioneer of modern dance in America.
How would you dance in a long scarf?
Fire Fountain, San Francisco Exposition
Arnold Genthe made a direct color photograph of the Fire Fountain at the 1915 Panama-Pacific Exposition in San Francisco. The fountain was lit with colored lights.
How would you make a fountain with fire?
French Soldiers Resting Among the Ruins
French soldiers rest on the rubble of a town in the war zone in 1916. Whole towns were destroyed by shelling in World War I.
Why do soldiers rest in ruins?
A Wave of Infantry Going Over the Top

Frank Hurley, who served as an official photographer with the Australian forces, photographed soldiers going over the top to resist a counterattack in 1917. He made composite pictures from several negatives to capture the drama.
Why was combining negatives controversial?
Boy Scouts, New York City, 1917
Underwood and Underwood photographed Boy Scouts in New York in 1917, when the Scouts were helping with the war effort. The picture was published in National Geographic.
What do Scouts do to help?
Dental Work in the Hospital, Hood Rubber Co.
Lewis Hine photographed dental work at the hospital of the Hood Rubber Company in Cambridge, Massachusetts, in 1917. Some factories offered health care to workers.
Why would a factory offer a dentist?
500 Newly Made Bluejackets
Underwood and Underwood photographed 500 newly made bluejackets, sailors of the U.S. Navy, in 1917. They had just joined up after the United States entered the war.
What would you wear as a sailor?
William Zorach
Man Ray photographed the artist William Zorach in 1917. Zorach was a Lithuanian-American sculptor and painter.
How does the photographer show his personality?
Jazz Band Leader Returns
Underwood and Underwood photographed a jazz band leader returning from World War I. Jim Europe's band introduced jazz to France.
What instruments does a jazz band play?
Carriers Gathering the Wounded Behind the Battle Line
Stretcher bearers collect wounded soldiers behind the lines in France in 1917. This is a photograph of the work of army medics.
What would a medic need to carry?
Machines of the Australian Flying Corps
This photograph shows airplanes of the Australian Flying Corps in 1918, lined up. Early airplanes were made of wood and fabric.
Why were they built from wood and cloth?
Vladivostok Parade, 1918
Allied troops paraded in the Russian port of Vladivostok in 1918. After the Russian Revolution, foreign soldiers came into the country.
Why would foreign troops march in Russia?
12-Inch Railway Howitzer Mark V
This photograph shows a British 12-inch railway howitzer, a huge gun that moved on rails in World War I. Such cannons could fire shells over many miles.
How would you move such a giant gun?
Montfaucon, Argonne
Edward Steichen was an aerial photographer in the U.S. Army in World War I. He photographed Montfaucon in the Argonne from the air in 1918, showing the shell-torn landscape.
Why would an army need pictures from the air?
Soldiers' Farewell Parade
A farewell parade for soldiers on their way to World War I fills a street in Indiana in 1918. The whole town came out to wave them off.
How would you say goodbye to someone going to war?
Genuine Jazz for the Yankee Wounded
American wounded soldiers listen to a jazz band in a Paris courtyard in 1918. Jazz was new to Europe, and soldiers loved it.
Why would music help the wounded?
German Prisoners Celebrating in London
German prisoners of war celebrate in a hospital prison camp near London in 1918. Even in captivity, prisoners kept up customs.
How would you celebrate if you were far from home?
A Baseball Game between the Shellshockers and the Gassers
Wounded American soldiers play baseball between the shellshockers and the gassers in London in 1918. They were recovering from war injuries and found comfort in a game.
Why would baseball help soldiers feel better?
Ali Kuli Khan
Georges Chevalier photographed Ali Kuli Khan, the chargé d'affaires of Persia in Washington, in 1919. He was a diplomat and a translator of Bahá'í texts.
What does a diplomat do?
Captain Eddie Rickenbacker
Captain Edward Rickenbacker was America's top ace of World War I, with 26 victories. He was a famous race car driver before flying.
How did pilots shoot in early airplanes?
The Nancy Crews Honored by Secretary Daniels

Underwood and Underwood photographed the crews of the Navy flying boats called NC, or Nancy, honored by Secretary of the Navy Josephus Daniels in 1919. They had made the first flight across the Atlantic.
How would you fly across an ocean in 1919?
A Woodstock Studio
This photograph shows an artist's studio in Woodstock, New York, around 1919. Woodstock became an art colony in the early 1900s.
What would you paint in a country studio?
Winter Sunshine, Woodstock, New York
A winter scene at Woodstock, New York, in 1919 shows sunlight on snowy hills. The art colony's artists loved the Catskill landscape.
What colors does winter sunshine have?
After a Snowstorm, Woodstock, New York
Snow weighs down branches and covers roofs at Woodstock, New York, in 1919. Photographs of snowy countryside were sold as postcards.
How do you clear snow from a roof?
The Country Beautiful, Woodstock, New York
A hillside near Woodstock, New York, in 1919 shows the Catskill landscape in leafy detail. The caption calls it The Country Beautiful.
What makes a place beautiful?
Across the Ranges, Woodstock, New York
This photograph looks across the ridges of the Catskills from Woodstock, New York, in 1919. Layers of hills fade into the distance.
How does distance change the colors?
The Turbine, Power-House, New York City
Lewis Hine photographed a workman beside a giant turbine in a New York power house around 1920. Hine began photographing men at work as a hero of the machine age.
How does a turbine make power?
André Honnorat
Auguste Léon made an autochrome of André Honnorat, a French politician, around 1920 for Albert Kahn's Archives of the Planet. Color portraits were rare then.
Why would a banker pay for color photographs?
Agave
Imogen Cunningham photographed an agave plant in close detail around 1920. She looked at plants as sculptures of line and light.
What shapes do the leaves make?
Blossom of Water Hyacinth
Imogen Cunningham photographed a water hyacinth blossom around 1920. Her plant pictures were praised for their sharp lines and soft tones.
What does a hyacinth blossom look like up close?
Edward B. Weston, M.D.
Edward Weston photographed his relative Dr. Edward B. Weston around 1920. Weston later became one of America's best-known photographers.
Why would someone photograph a relative?
Bell Ringer Outside a Church
Doris Ulmann photographed a bell ringer outside a church. Ulmann was a New York portrait photographer who traveled in the South and the Appalachians to photograph vanishing ways of life.
What does a bell ringer do?
Man with Bridle
Doris Ulmann photographed a man holding a bridle, the strap for guiding a horse, around 1920. Her soft-focus portraits are quiet and respectful.
How does a bridle control a horse?
Absinthe House, New Orleans
Arnold Genthe photographed the Absinthe House, an old bar in New Orleans's French Quarter, around 1920. The building dates from the early 1800s.
What does an old building say about its city?
Janet Flanner

Berenice Abbott photographed Janet Flanner, an American writer in Paris who wrote for The New Yorker, in the 1920s. Abbott made portraits of artists in Paris before she turned to documenting New York.
What is a Paris correspondent?
Old Man with Boy
Doris Ulmann photographed an old man with a boy around 1920. A grandfather and grandson are a favorite portrait.
What would an old man teach a boy?
First American Olympic Hockey Team
The Tri-State News Bureau photographed the first American Olympic ice hockey team in 1920 at the Antwerp Games. Hockey was added to the Summer Olympics that year.
Why would hockey be in the summer Games?
Arlington National Cemetery Amphitheater
Theodor Horydczak photographed the Memorial Amphitheater at Arlington National Cemetery in Virginia in the 1920s. It holds ceremonies for the nation's fallen soldiers.
Why would a country keep a cemetery for soldiers?
Eisenhower Farm at Gettysburg
Theodor Horydczak photographed a farm outside Gettysburg, Pennsylvania, in the 1920s. Later, President Dwight Eisenhower retired to a farm there.
Why would a president want to live on a farm?
Aerial View of the Washington Post Office and Railroad Station
An early aerial photograph shows Washington's main post office and Union Station, 1920. Airplanes made new views of cities possible.
What does a city look like from above?
Repairing Telephone Lines During a Gas Attack
Keystone View Company photographed signal soldiers with gas masks repairing a telephone line during a gas attack on the Western Front. Communication wires were cut constantly.
Why would a telephone line matter so much?
Drilling for a Shot: Old-Fashioned Way of Mining Coal
Lewis Hine photographed a coal miner drilling a hole for explosives in 1921. Mining was hard and dangerous work done mostly by hand.
How would you drill rock by hand?
Attic
Edward Weston photographed the interior of an attic in 1921 with beams and angles in light and shadow. He was moving toward sharp-focus, simple compositions.
How do light and shadow make shapes in a room?
Alexander Kerensky
Georges Chevalier photographed Alexander Kerensky, the head of Russia's provisional government in 1917. After the revolution he lived in exile.
What would you do if you lost your country?
Gift
Man Ray's 1921 photograph shows a flat iron with tacks glued to its bottom. He called it Gift, and it is one of the most famous objects in Dada art.
Why would you ruin an iron?
David F. Houston
Lewis Hine photographed David F. Houston, a U.S. cabinet member, in 1921. Hine also made portraits for a living.
What does a cabinet member do?
Alexandre Khatissian
Auguste Léon photographed Alexandre Khatissian, a prime minister of Armenia, in 1921 as part of Albert Kahn's Archives of the Planet. Léon recorded delegates at the Paris peace conference.
What does a peace conference do?
Akaki Chkhenkeli
Auguste Léon photographed Akaki Chkhenkeli, a Georgian statesman, in 1921. Léon recorded delegates who came to Paris.
Why would delegates come to Paris?
Dedication of the Liberty Memorial Site, Kansas City
In November 1921, a huge crowd gathered in Kansas City, Missouri, to dedicate the site of the Liberty Memorial. Allied military leaders from five countries attended.
Why would a city build a memorial?
Dog Funeral, Washington
A woman named Selma Snook held a funeral for her dog in Washington in 1921. The newspaper photographer made it a funny but sad image.
How would you remember a pet?
Spring Fashion Show, New York
Women's clothing is modeled at a spring fashion show in New York in 1921. The hemlines and hats show the fashion of the early 1920s.
How is the clothing different from today's?
Gable and Apples
Alfred Stieglitz photographed the gable of a house and apple trees at Lake George, New York, in 1922. His pictures of the farm there were quiet and detailed.
How do the apples and the gable fit together?
Barn, Lake George
Alfred Stieglitz photographed a barn at Lake George in 1922. He spent summers on the family estate there and photographed what he saw around him.
What do you notice about the barn's shape?
Armco Steel, Ohio
Edward Weston photographed the huge steel plant of Armco in Middletown, Ohio, in 1922. The photograph made smokestacks look like monuments and led him to a new modern style.
How can a factory look beautiful?
Alice B. Toklas and Gertrude Stein
Man Ray photographed the writer Gertrude Stein and her partner Alice B. Toklas in Paris in 1922. Their apartment was a gathering place for artists and writers.
Why do artists like to meet and talk?
Easter Egg Rolling at the White House
Children roll Easter eggs on the White House lawn in 1922. The Easter egg roll has been a tradition for over a century.
What would you do at an egg roll?
Dedication of the Lincoln Memorial, 1922
The Lincoln Memorial in Washington, D.C., was dedicated on May 30, 1922, in front of a big crowd. Robert Todd Lincoln, Abraham Lincoln's son, attended.
Why would the president's son attend?
William Livingstone, Jr.
The Detroit Photographic Company photographed William Livingstone Jr., a Detroit businessman, in 1922. Portraits of important local people were part of the business.
Why would a photographer make portraits of businessmen?
Advertising Hosiery on Live Models
A shop in Washington used live models to show off hosiery, or stockings, in 1922. Women stood in the window and drew a crowd.
How else would a store advertise?
The Great White South
Herbert Ponting's 1923 book The Great White South told of the 1910 to 1913 Terra Nova expedition to Antarctica. This picture from the book shows the ice and sky.
What would you photograph at the bottom of the world?
The Great White South, Antarctic Scene
Herbert Ponting's pictures of Antarctica from Captain Scott's expedition were published in a book in 1923. Ponting made some of the most famous pictures of the polar regions.
What would you write in a polar diary?
President Coolidge on the Speaker's Stand
President Calvin Coolidge speaks from a stand with Army and Navy officers in 1923. Coolidge was known as Silent Cal because he spoke so little.
Why would a quiet president be a good speaker?
Entrance to a Yurok Sweat-House
Edward S. Curtis photographed the entrance of a Yurok sweat house in California around 1923. The house was a low dwelling used by men for gathering and ceremony.
Why would a sweat house have a small entrance?
Equivalent
Alfred Stieglitz photographed clouds in the sky for a series called Equivalents in the mid-1920s. He called them equivalents because they were equal to feelings, not pictures of things.
What feeling does a cloud give you?
Diego Rivera
Edward Weston photographed the Mexican painter Diego Rivera in 1924 when Weston was living in Mexico City. Rivera was known for giant murals.
Why would a painter paint on a huge wall?
Victorious Olympic Team Returns Aboard the S.S. America
Members of the American team, victorious at the 1924 Paris Olympics, return aboard the S.S. America. The crowd on deck wave flags and hats.
What would you do on the ship home from the Olympics?
Fête du Trône
Eugène Atget photographed a fairground at the Fête du Trône in Paris around 1925. The funfair set up each spring on the edge of the city.
What rides would be at a fair in 1925?
Plaster Works, Los Angeles
Edward Weston photographed a plaster works in Los Angeles in 1925 with a close eye for shapes. He found beauty in factories and machines.
What shapes can you see?
Italian Delegation, Locarno Conference
Roger Dumas made an autochrome, an early color picture, of the Italian delegation at the Locarno Conference in 1925. European powers met at Locarno in Switzerland to try to keep peace.
How could color photographs have helped in 1925?
204 Rue du Château des Rentiers
Eugène Atget photographed a shop window on Rue du Château des Rentiers in Paris around 1925. He took photographs of shop windows, mannequins and displays.
What would you put in a shop window?
Magnolia Blossom
Imogen Cunningham photographed a magnolia blossom in 1925. She isolated the flower against a dark background so it looks like a sculpture.
What does a magnolia blossom remind you of?
French Delegation, Locarno Conference
Roger Dumas made an autochrome of the French delegation at the Locarno Conference in 1925. The color glows softly in the picture.
How does early color look different?
Boutique, Marché aux Halles, Paris
Eugène Atget photographed a shop at the old market of Les Halles in Paris around 1925. The market fed the city for centuries.
What would you buy at a market stall?
Ruth St. Denis
Doris Ulmann photographed the dancer Ruth St. Denis around 1925. St. Denis helped found modern dance in the United States.
How do dancers tell stories without words?
Two Callas
Imogen Cunningham photographed two calla lilies in 1925. The simple shapes and sharp light make the flowers look like sculpture.
How are the two flowers different?
Polish Delegation, Locarno Conference
Roger Dumas made an autochrome of the Polish delegation at the Locarno Conference in 1925. Men in dark coats stand in a garden.
What would you wear to an important meeting?
German Delegation, Locarno Conference
Roger Dumas made an autochrome of the German delegation at Locarno in 1925. Germany joined the agreements to keep peace in Europe.
Why would former enemies sign agreements?
